slides.title: Cut it finer
slides.text: A customer wants half a cake, but the tray only holds fourths. Tally cuts each half into two fourths, and the share has not changed at all.

visual.label: Half a cake re-sliced: 1/2 and 2/4 cover exactly the same share

focus.cue: Half a cake: 1 of 2 equal parts.
Cut each part in two: 2 of 4 parts. The share has not moved.

slides.title: Re-slicing keeps value
slides.text: Cutting every piece into 2 smaller pieces doubles both numbers: 1/2 becomes 2/4. The pieces shrink, the count grows, the share stays the same.

slides.title: Rough first, then compare
slides.text: Rough first: 5/8 is a little more than 1/2. Compare it with 3/4 using the halfway mark as your referee.

visual.label: Comparing 5/8 and 3/4 on the same whole: 3/4 is 6/8, one eighth more

focus.cue: 5/8 sits one eighth past the halfway line.
3/4 is 6/8: one eighth more, so 3/4 is greater.

slides.title: Same whole, or no contest
slides.text: A fraction only has a size inside its whole. Half of a tiny cake can be less cake than a fourth of a huge one. Compare shares of the same whole.

slides.title: Stretch: Any number of cuts
slides.text: Re-slicing works with any count. Cut each third into 3 and 2/3 becomes 6/9: same share, three times the pieces, three times the count.

words.means: different fractions that name the same share
a known share, like 1/2, used to judge other shares
to decide which of two amounts is greater, or if they match
the one full thing a fraction is a share of

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Fraction Factory at Re-Slice, then serve the orders. Re-slice a share before you decide if two orders match.
